lines.t: Listen to an announcement by an instructor in a classroom.

I'd like to announce that our guest, Professor Alissa Shevchuk from the History Department, has moved her lecture up from the eleventh to the fourth. This means she'll be joining us in class next Wednesday. Please click on the link in your syllabus to read Professor Shevchuk's article on nineteenth-century European nationalism in preparation for the discussion. Visit my office hours or email me by Monday if there are any aspects of the article that you'd like Professor Shevchuk to address in detail.

o-t6-linton.title: TPO6 Announcement — Georgia Linton
o-t6-linton.note: 스크린샷 스크립트로 재구성, 원본 음원 아님

lines.t: Listen to an announcement on a university radio station.

Attention everyone. Due to unforeseen circumstances, the appearance of Georgia Linton has been postponed. The event will now take place next Tuesday at seven p.m. in the same location. Come hear her read from her widely acclaimed collection of poems called Seasons That Never Spoke. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause and appreciate your understanding. If you have any questions, please contact the head of the English Department.

o-t6-conformity.title: TPO6 Social Sciences Talk — social conformity
o-t6-conformity.note: 스크린샷 스크립트로 재구성, 원본 음원 아님

lines.t: Listen to a talk on a social sciences podcast.

In everyday life, people often find themselves adjusting their thoughts or actions based on what others around them are doing. This tendency to align with group behavior is called social conformity and has been a fascinating subject for researchers in psychology. One classic study from the 1950s, led by psychologist Solomon Asch, explored how individuals respond when their own perceptions differ from those of a group. In the experiment, participants were shown a set of lines and asked to identify which one matched a reference line in length. What the real participants weren't told was that others in their group were actually actors who intentionally gave the same incorrect answers. Surprisingly, many participants chose to go along with the group's answer, even when it was clearly wrong—highlighting how group influence can sometimes override personal judgment. While this can lead to questionable decisions, the tendency to align with others is hard-wired into human behavior for a good reason. In many social contexts, it can foster a sense of unity and shared understanding. It helps people feel connected and reinforces group identity. Now let's talk about why this has been of critical importance to people throughout the history of humanity.

o-t6-commute.title: TPO6 Conversation — commuting and moving
o-t6-commute.note: 스크린샷 스크립트로 재구성, 원본 음원 아님

lines.t: I've had it with this commute. I don't mind riding the train, but I hate having to get up at five a.m. every day.
Why don't you find an apartment closer to work?
I've actually checked rental listings online. There are some good options a few blocks from the office, but I'm not sure about this neighborhood. It seems like a pretty dull place to live.
You know, Mark's lived here for years. Ask him what he thinks of it.
That's not a bad idea. I'll see if he has time to chat after the client meeting this afternoon.

o-t6-organisms.title: TPO6 Life Sciences Talk — relationships between organisms
o-t6-organisms.note: 스크린샷 스크립트로 재구성, 원본 음원 아님

lines.t: Listen to a talk on a life sciences podcast.

In nature, organisms interact in various ways. Long-term interactions between two different species can be mutualistic, commensalistic, or parasitic. A mutualistic relationship is when it's beneficial for both species. A classic case is the relationship between bees and flowers. Bees collect nectar from flowers for food. As they do so, the bees inadvertently help flowers pollinate. Pollination is the process of transferring plants' reproductive material—the pollen—from plant to plant, which is essential for plant reproduction. Commensalism involves one species benefiting, while the other is neither helped nor harmed. An example is when a type of small sea animal, called a barnacle, attaches itself to whales. The barnacles benefit from this in several ways, such as by catching a ride to places in the ocean where food is abundant. You see, whales feed on microorganisms called plankton by filtering them out of the water. And so do barnacles, which reach plankton-rich areas while being attached to the whale. The barnacles benefit from their relationship with the whale, while the whale remains unaffected. Parasitism occurs when one species benefits at the expense of the other. An example is the relationship between mammals and the insects we call ticks. Ticks feed on a mammal's blood. The blood loss can be significant for the mammal and could potentially cause anemia. Anemia is when the blood has a reduced capacity for carrying oxygen and can cause fatigue and weakness.

o-t6-harlem.title: TPO6 History Talk — Harlem Renaissance
o-t6-harlem.note: 스크린샷 스크립트로 재구성, 원본 음원 아님 (화면 오타 knows → known 으로 읽음)

lines.t: Listen to a talk on a history podcast.

In the 1920s, the cultural phenomenon known as the Harlem Renaissance transformed the New York neighborhood of Harlem into a cultural epicenter. It sparked a wave of innovation in music, literature, and theater. One of the most exciting developments was the rise of jazz music. Jazz musicians like Louis Armstrong brought improvisation to the forefront—transforming simple melodies into spontaneous, expressive performances. It was like watching a painter create a masterpiece in real time, each note a brushstroke of emotion and skill. Literature also flourished. Poet Langston Hughes became a defining voice of the era. His poetry often echoed the rhythms of jazz—he wrote in short, rhythmic lines that felt musical even when read aloud. Theater saw a surge of grassroots creativity. The Krigwa Players, founded in Harlem in 1925, were a pioneering theater group that performed original one-act plays by emerging playwrights. The Krigwa Players staged productions in community centers and libraries to reach local audiences who might not have access to formal theaters. These venues allowed them to keep costs low, foster community involvement, and ensure that theater remained a shared, inclusive experience—rooted in everyday life.

originals.passage:
Subject: Upcoming enhancements to project management software

Dear Mr. Tanaka,

I hope this message finds you well. I'm writing to inform you of upcoming updates to our project management software, scheduled to go live next Thursday. These enhancements are designed to improve user experience.

Key improvements include
– Customizable dashboards for personalized project views and streamlined task tracking
– A redesigned, more intuitive user interface for easier navigation
– Addition of collaboration tools, including real-time editing and integrated messaging, to support seamless teamwork

Please note that a scheduled system downtime will occur from 2:00 A.M. to 4:00 A.M. (local time) on Thursday to implement these changes. We recommend informing your team and adjusting any time-sensitive activities accordingly. If you have any questions or need support during the transition, our team is ready to assist.

Regards,
Lisa Chen
originals.stem: It can be inferred that the current software lacks which of the following?
options: The ability to track tasks different team members are assigned to perform
The ability for team members to contact one another within the same system
A user interface for navigation
A way to inform users of tasks
originals.evidence: Addition of collaboration tools, including real-time editing and integrated messaging
originals.trap: 메일에 task tracking이 나와 task 관련 기능이 없다고 이어 붙임. 하지만 tracking은 개선(streamlined)되는 기능일 뿐
originals.diff: lacks는 '지금 없다'는 뜻이라, 'Addition of'로 새로 추가되는 기능인 integrated messaging(시스템 안 메시지)이 답. streamlined/redesigned는 이미 있는 기능을 고친 것
originals.rule: 'lacks'를 묻는 추론은 Addition/new가 붙은 기능만 후보다. improved/redesigned는 이미 있는 것

originals.passage:
Bioluminescence is a fascinating phenomenon, whereby living organisms produce light through chemical reactions. This ability is found in a wide variety of species, including certain bacteria, fungi, insects, and marine animals. The light produced can serve several purposes, such as attracting mates, deterring predators, or luring prey.

One of the most well-known bioluminescent organisms is the firefly, which uses light to communicate with potential mates. However, bioluminescence is most common in the marine environment. For example, the anglerfish has a bioluminescent lure that it uses to attract prey in the deep ocean. Similarly, some species of squid and jellyfish exhibit bioluminescence to escape predators by confusing or startling them.
originals.stem: What purpose does bioluminescence serve for fireflies?
options: It frightens predators.
It aids in reproduction.
It lures prey.
It helps them escape from danger.
originals.evidence: the firefly, which uses light to communicate with potential mates
originals.trap: luring prey도 지문에 실제로 있음 — 하지만 anglerfish의 목적
originals.diff: firefly는 짝(mates)과 소통하니 reproduction. 먹이(prey) 유인은 anglerfish, 포식자(predators) 관련은 squid·jellyfish
originals.rule: 목적이 여러 개 나오는 지문은 생물마다 한 줄씩 짝지어 두고, 질문한 생물의 줄만 본다
originals.causeAI: 다른 생물(anglerfish)의 목적을 firefly에 붙임 — TPO6 L8(barnacles)과 같은 실수

originals.evidence: The enzyme luciferase, which catalyzes the light-producing reaction
originals.trap: 같은 문장 뒤쪽에 visualizing이 나와 겉보기에 겹침 (AI 추정)
originals.diff: 효소(enzyme)가 반응(reaction)을 catalyze한다는 건 일으키거나 촉진한다는 뜻이라 initiates. visualize(시각화)는 이미징 활용을 설명하는 말
originals.rule: Vocabulary 선택지가 같은 문장에 그대로 보이면 함정부터 의심한다 — 주어와 목적어(효소가 반응을) 관계로 뜻을 정한다

originals.evidence: You know, Mark's lived here for years. Ask him what he thinks of it.
originals.trap: time to chat이 남자의 마지막 말에 나와서
originals.diff: 질문은 여자가 암시한 것을 묻는다. 여자는 '오래 살았으니 물어봐라', 즉 의견이 있을 거라고 말함. 'I'll see if he has time'은 남자 말이고, 시간이 없다는 뜻도 아님
originals.rule: 'What does the woman suggest'는 여자의 말만 본다. I'll see if…는 '되는지 알아보겠다'이지 안 된다는 말이 아님
originals.causeAI: 다른 사람의 말을 가져왔고, '알아보겠다'를 '안 된다'로 지나치게 추론함

originals.set: Life Sciences Talk — relationships between organisms
originals.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?
options: How organisms protect themselves from other organisms
How environmental changes affect animals' feeding and reproduction
Benefits of studying species in their natural environment
Types of relationships between living organisms
originals.evidence: Long-term interactions between two different species can be mutualistic, commensalistic, or parasitic.
originals.trap: 기생(at the expense of)·피해 이야기에서 '방어'를 떠올렸을 것 (AI 추정)
originals.diff: 도입에서 세 가지 종류(mutualistic / commensalistic / parasitic)를 제시하므로 강의 주제는 관계의 종류. 보호 행동은 나오지 않음
originals.rule: 도입에서 '~ can be A, B, or C'처럼 종류를 나누면 그 분류 자체가 Main Idea
originals.causeAI: 도입부에서 종류를 나누는 신호를 놓침 (이 강의 0/4 — 졸았는지는 기록 없음)

originals.set: Life Sciences Talk — relationships between organisms
originals.stem: Why does the speaker discuss plant pollination?
options: To introduce new research on how plants reproduce
To explain how both organisms can benefit from their interaction
To contrast various methods of pollination in plants
To identify a similarity between mutualistic and parasitic relationships
originals.evidence: A mutualistic relationship is when it's beneficial for both species. A classic case is the relationship between bees and flowers.
originals.trap: pollination이 선택지에 그대로 있음 — 하지만 그건 예시의 '내용'
originals.diff: pollination은 상리공생(둘 다 이익)의 대표 예(classic case). 여러 수분 방법을 비교하는 내용은 없음
originals.rule: Why discuss X 문제는 X 바로 앞(A classic case is…)을 보고 무엇의 예인지로 답한다
originals.causeAI: 예시의 역할이 아니라 예시에 나온 단어로 고름

originals.set: Life Sciences Talk — relationships between organisms
originals.stem: What does the speaker point out about barnacles' food?
options: It is the same as whales' food.
It is most plentiful in oxygen-rich areas of the ocean.
It requires a long time to be filtered out of the water.
It is often found attached to whales.
originals.evidence: whales feed on microorganisms called plankton by filtering them out of the water. And so do barnacles
originals.trap: attached to whales도 실제로 나옴 — 하지만 고래에 붙는 건 따개비 자신
originals.diff: And so do barnacles는 '따개비도 플랑크톤을 먹는다', 즉 고래와 먹이가 같다는 뜻. 고래에 붙어 있는 것은 먹이가 아니라 따개비 자신
originals.rule: 'X's food'처럼 무엇의 무엇을 묻는 질문은 주인(따개비)과 대상(먹이)을 나눠 본다. 'And so do + 주어'는 앞 문장 동사를 되풀이하는 말
originals.causeAI: 따개비의 특징을 따개비 먹이의 특징으로 착각 — R6(firefly와 anglerfish)과 같은 실수

originals.set: Life Sciences Talk — relationships between organisms
originals.stem: What possible effect of ticks on mammals is mentioned by the speaker?
options: The mammal may start feeling tired and weak
The mammal may need more food to survive.
The mammal may experience mild skin irritation.
Harmful microorganisms may enter the mammal's blood.
originals.evidence: Anemia is when the blood has a reduced capacity for carrying oxygen and can cause fatigue and weakness.
originals.trap: '피를 잃으면 먹이가 더 필요하겠다'는 상식적 추론
originals.diff: 강의의 인과: 진드기 때문에 피를 잃고, 빈혈이 생겨 피로·쇠약(fatigue and weakness)해진다. 먹이가 더 필요하다는 말은 없음
originals.rule: 'mentioned' 질문은 원인과 결과의 마지막 단계를 들은 그대로 고른다. 상식으로 만든 결과는 버린다
originals.causeAI: 들은 내용이 아니라 상식으로 결과를 만들어 냄

originals.stem: Why does the speaker mention a painter creating a masterpiece in real time?
options: To illustrate how jazz musicians improvised during performances
To suggest that jazz musicians often worked together with painters
To highlight how quickly jazz music gained popularity
To show how painters influenced jazz musicians' style
originals.evidence: brought improvisation to the forefront—transforming simple melodies into spontaneous, expressive performances. It was like watching a painter create a masterpiece in real time
originals.trap: 화가와 재즈 음악가가 같은 문장에 나와서 실제로 함께 일한 것으로 읽음
originals.diff: It was like…는 비유다. 즉흥연주(improvisation)를 '실시간으로 그림 그리기'에 빗댄 것. 실제로 함께 작업했다는 말은 없음
originals.rule: It was like / just as / imagine은 비유 신호. 목적은 바로 앞 개념을 설명(illustrate)하는 것

originals.stem: What does the speaker say about some poems of Langston Hughes?
options: They have inspired theatrical performances.
They sound like jazz music when read.
They praise the music of Louis Armstrong.
They were written with the help of a musician.
originals.evidence: His poetry often echoed the rhythms of jazz—he wrote in short, rhythmic lines that felt musical even when read aloud.
originals.diff: Hughes의 특징은 재즈 리듬의 시(felt musical when read aloud). 연극은 Krigwa Players 이야기
originals.rule: 음악·문학·연극처럼 분야마다 인물이 나오면 '인물: 특징'을 한 줄씩 적고, 다른 줄의 단어가 섞인 선택지는 지운다
